analysis.title: Spooky Charts: What Could Investors Be Missing?
key_insights: Bond yields have climbed to multi-year peaks, ending the decade-long regime of cheap money and suppressed yields, while broader equity markets, particularly in the US, show high investor complacency.

US household equity allocations are at proportions rarely seen in modern market history while valuation multiples approach dot-com levels. Redwheel says this may leave portfolios with little liquidity buffer to absorb shocks.

Global cash held by non-bank investors is at its lowest level in roughly three decades, leaving little cushion against drawdowns or to buy mispriced assets in a panic (source cited: J.P. Morgan Flows & Liquidity).

Balance sheet leverage of the top 15 hedge funds has doubled in the past decade, which Redwheel describes as essentially maxing out capacity. Crowded, heavily geared trades can lead to rapid deleveraging after modest market moves (source cited: Federal Reserve Financial Stability Report, May 2026).
The top 10 US companies are roughly 40% of the S&P 500, all in technology. Excluding 485 S&P 500 companies would still leave the remaining heavyweights keeping the index above its 2020 peak.

Forward 12-month capex estimates for Alphabet, Amazon, Microsoft, Meta and Oracle continue to rise and are a multiple of what they spent five years ago. The dollar total is missing from the extracted text.
Redwheel cites railroads and the dot-com telecom buildout as precedents where concentrated infrastructure spending was followed by overcapacity, price deflation and depressed shareholder returns.

Redwheel believes the winners of the past decade are unlikely to repeat over the next ten years. It suggests diversifying toward value, owning businesses with strong balance sheets that trade at substantial discounts to intrinsic worth (Redwheel Global Intrinsic Value strategy, which the note promotes).

sector_views.rationale: Redwheel flags concentration risk, with the top 10 US companies (all technology) at about 40% of the S&P 500, and rising AI capex as a possible overbuild. It does not state a formal sector rating.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Higher yields end the cheap-money regime that supported equity valuations. No numeric level is given.

risk_factors: Valuation multiples near dot-com levels combined with record retail equity allocations.
Minimal cash buffers among non-bank investors globally.
Hedge fund leverage at elevated levels, which raises deleveraging risk.
Index concentration in ten technology names.
Possible AI infrastructure overcapacity and price deflation after heavy capex.
vol_and_positioning: Non-bank investor cash allocation is at roughly a three-decade low (J.P. Morgan Flows & Liquidity, as of 1 July 2026).
Top 15 hedge fund balance sheet leverage has doubled in a decade (Fed Financial Stability Report, May 2026).
The note includes a chart of 3-month realised correlation, S&P 500 vs S&P 500 Equal Weight (Chart 4). The text gives no reading from it.
